title: Your first 30 days: what they are for
body_md:
A new kingdom spends roughly its first 85–100 days preparing for its first KvK: pre-KvK (Eve of the Crusade) starts around day 85–95 and KvK1 around day 100 [B01-0500]. Your first 30 days are the first third of that runway. You do not need to master the game in them. You need three things:

1. **Habits that add up**: daily streaks and full queues, started from day 1.
2. **A safe home**: an active alliance [A06-0516].
3. **Understanding**: one concept per stretch, so the menus stop being noise.

**How this guide is laid out.** Five stretches: days 1–3, 4–7, 8–14, 15–21 and 22–30. Each has a *Goals* block (3–5 goals) and a *Concept* block (one idea, explained). The stretch boundaries are a pacing aid for learning, not game timings. No source says which City Hall level a new player reaches on a given day (gap PROPOSED-CH-BY-KINGDOM-DAY), so goals are tied to City Hall levels or to dated kingdom events, never to "be CH X by day Y". If you are faster or slower, follow your City Hall, not the calendar.

**Safe to ignore for now** (each with its reason):
- Buildings that are not on the City Hall chain, such as extra resource buildings or the Watchtower [A01-0007].
- Using gems to finish buildings or research instantly [A04-0009].
- Spreading sculptures across many commanders: finish one first [A06-0500], and keep universal (gold) legendary sculptures for one long-term legendary [A06-0510].

This guide is shorter than the F2P guide and does not repeat it. Where a topic goes deeper, it says *see the F2P guide* and gives the block id.
why_md: A brand-new player meets dozens of menus in the first hour, and most of them can wait. Anchoring the month to KvK1 [B01-0500] explains both why the early days matter (they are the cheapest time to start streaks and join an alliance) and why they don't need to be perfect (about two thirds of the preparation time is still ahead when this guide ends).
uncertain_notes: We deliberately give no City Hall or troop-tier target for day 30. The only source for one is a weak 2026 player report, not used here; see the F2P guide's budget block for it.

title: Days 1–3 goals: alliance, civilization, City Hall, two streaks
body_md:
**Goals**
1. **Join an active alliance** as soon as one accepts you. Its members' helps shorten your construction, research and healing timers [A10-0006], and alliance gift chests generated by spenders are a major source of sculptures, keys and VIP points for non-spenders [A06-0516]. How to pick one: see the New Kingdom guide (`nk-pick-alliance-checklist`).
2. **Pick a civilization without agonising.** China is the most recommended start (+5% building speed, +5% AP recovery, Sun Tzu as starting commander) [A14-0003]. The choice is not final: reaching City Hall 10 gives one free Civilization Change [A14-0002].
3. **Upgrade City Hall and only the buildings it requires**; everything else waits [A01-0007]. The concept block for this stretch explains why.
4. **Start two daily streaks today.** Claim the free VIP points every day: 40 on day 1, +20 per consecutive day, up to 200 a day; a missed day resets the streak to 40 [A05-0003]. And reach 100 points in Daily Objectives for the chest with 100 gems; it resets daily at 00:00 UTC [A04-0001].
5. **Keep nothing worth stealing when you log off.** Resources kept as items cannot be plundered, and gems cannot be plundered in any form [A03-0007]. More in the F2P guide (`d0-day1-survival`). Beginner protection and shield numbers are still pending in-game measurement (see `nk-day1-protection-pending`).
why_md: The alliance and the two streaks are the goals that get worse the later you start: the VIP streak restarts at 40 when a day is missed [A05-0003], and the 100-gem chest is the only daily, guaranteed gem source that sources found [A04-0001]. The civilization goal is here only to stop new players from stalling on it, because a free change comes at City Hall 10 [A14-0002].

title: Concept for days 1–3: City Hall is the gate
body_md:
**One rule explains most of the city screen:** no building can be upgraded above your City Hall level [A01-0003]. City Hall level is the ceiling of your whole city.

**City Hall has its own requirements.** From CH3, City Hall level N needs the Wall at level N−1 plus one other building at N−1. That other building rotates: Hospital, Scout Camp, Storehouse, Barracks, Alliance Center, Academy, Archery Range, Trading Post, Stable, Siege Workshop [A01-0001]. Some of those have prerequisites of their own. For example, from level 5 the Wall needs the Tavern at the same level, and at higher levels the Tavern needs the Quarry [A01-0004].

**What City Hall gives you in a first month's range** [A01-0001, A01-0002, A01-0011]:
- **CH5:** a 2nd march.
- **CH8:** Tier 2 troops and the queue dashboard; upgrade reward 2× 8h universal speedups.
- **CH9:** upgrade reward 1× 24h universal speedup.
- **CH10:** Lyceum of Wisdom; upgrade reward one Civilization Change.
- **CH11:** a 3rd march.

**The habit to build:** before you start any upgrade, ask "is this on the path to my next City Hall?" If not, it can wait [A01-0007].
why_md: Beginners lose builder time on buildings that look important but don't raise the ceiling. Once the gate rule is clear, the build menu shrinks to one chain. Raw build times grow quickly (CH10 is listed at 22h raw and CH16 at 4d) [A01-0001], so builder time becomes the scarcest early resource.
uncertain_notes: Raw times come from the Fandom developer dataset and have no in-game confirmation yet (L-A01-02); real times depend on your buffs (L-A01-03). Some early unlock levels are disputed between sources (L-A01-01), so this block lists only the uncontested ones.

title: Days 4–7 goals: second builder, barbarians, the Pelagius decision
body_md:
**Goals**
1. **Keep a second builder running.** You start with one building queue. Builder Recruitment items open a second one for 2 days each, and they stack; VIP 6 makes it permanent [A01-0006]. Point both builders at the City Hall chain.
2. **Fight barbarians with your regenerating AP every day.** They give commander EXP, resources and Daily Objective tasks [A09-0007]. At kingdom opening only barbarians Lv1–6 exist; higher levels unlock kingdom-wide over the following days, and you must beat each level before you can attack the next [A09-0004].
3. **Decide about Legendary Pelagius before spending anything on him.** Since 1.1.09 an event lets you upgrade Pelagius from Epic to Legendary, available from day 5 in new kingdoms [C04-0005]. Opinion on his value is divided [A06-0508]; see the F2P guide (`d4-pelagius-day5`).
4. **Use the 2nd march as soon as City Hall 5 unlocks it** [A03-0023], for example to keep a gatherer on the map. Resources for the City Hall path come from gathering [A01-0007].
5. **Help your allies every day.** Helping 20 times is worth 10 Daily Objective points [A10-0006].
why_md: Builder time and AP are both use-it-or-lose-it: an empty queue and AP sitting at the cap are progress you never get back [A09-0007]. Pelagius is the first dated decision in a new kingdom [C04-0005], and the first place a beginner can spend heavily on something the sources disagree about [A06-0508].
uncertain_notes: A06-0508 (Pelagius value) is low confidence and the sources are divided. C04-0005 is a patch-state card (official 1.1.09 note, status bruto). The kingdom-wide barbarian unlock schedule by day is unknown (L-A09-05).

title: Concept for days 4–7: Action Points (AP)
body_md:
**What AP is.** Action Points are the fuel for attacking barbarians. One attack costs 50 AP, and 2 AP less for each consecutive attack by the same commander without returning to the city, down to 40 [A09-0002].

**The cap.** You hold at most 1,500 AP without buffs, and AP regenerates over time [A09-0001]. Regeneration you don't spend is wasted at the cap, so the first rule is: **spend regenerating AP every day** [A09-0007].

**Free AP and AP items.** Every day you can claim a Daily Action Points bonus: 500 AP in the official notes of 2020, and since 1.1.02 it can push you above the cap [A09-0001, C04-0032]. The 60-point Daily Objectives chest also gives one 100-AP item a day [A09-0006]. Items can be kept for later, so the second rule is: **save AP items for events that pay more per AP**, Lohar's Trial first and, much later, Eve of the Crusade before KvK1 [A11-0505, A09-0007].

**Automation.** The game has a built-in auto-peacekeeping feature that hunts barbarians for you; third-party scripts are penalised through the Conduct Score [A09-0008]. Use the built-in one, never a bot.
why_md: AP is the first resource a beginner sees run out, and the first one wasted without notice. Two rules (never sit at the cap; save the items) cover most of it. The F2P guide has the deeper version (`d0-ap-discipline`).
uncertain_notes: C04-0032 is a patch-state card (official 1.1.02 note, status bruto). The 500 AP daily claim is the 2020 value; the 2026 amount is unconfirmed (L-A09-02). The base regeneration rate per hour is unknown (L-A09-01), and so is the auto-peacekeeping unlock level (L-A09-04).

title: Days 8–14 goals: dashboard, Academy, gathering, the CH10 choices
body_md:
**Goals** (tied to City Hall levels; which day you reach them is not measured, PROPOSED-CH-BY-KINGDOM-DAY)
1. **From City Hall 8, refill everything from the queue dashboard at every login**: construction, training, research, healing, scouting and alliance donations from one screen [A01-0011].
2. **Academy: economy and speed techs first** (Writing, Masonry, Engineering, Mathematics), before military ones [A02-0500]. For the later order, see the F2P guide (`d4-research-economy`, `d15-research-military`).
3. **Gather inside alliance territory** (+25% speed) [A03-0009]. When online, use the nearest node; before logging off, send marches to large nodes so they don't come home early [A03-0016].
4. **At City Hall 10, two new things.** The free Civilization Change arrives as an upgrade reward [A01-0002]: use it only if you planned a switch [A14-0002]. And the Lyceum of Wisdom opens Peerless Scholar: one mock exam each weekday, plus a preliminary and a final every two weeks whose passers split a gem pool [A10-0005].
5. **Claim the free Tavern chests daily**: 3 silver chests a day at Tavern 1–4, more as the Tavern levels up, and a free golden chest every 3 days at Tavern 1, shortening at higher levels [A10-0003].
why_md: From CH8 the game hands you a tool that saves time at every login (the dashboard [A01-0011]), and from CH10 one that pays gems (Peerless Scholar [A10-0005]). Economy research early shortens every later timer [A02-0500], and gathering in territory is a free 25% [A03-0009].
uncertain_notes: The ordered research path with times is a known gap (L-A02-01). The size of the Peerless Scholar gem pool is unknown (L-A04-05).

title: Concept for days 8–14: what the alliance actually does for you
body_md:
**Help = time.** Allies can help your construction, research and healing; each help fills 1% of the progress bar. How many helps one job can receive depends on your Alliance Center level: 5 at level 1, 18 at level 14, 30 at level 25. Troop training cannot be helped [A10-0006].

**Territory = gathering speed.** Gathering at normal resource points inside your alliance's territory is 25% faster and also adds resources to the alliance storehouse [A03-0009].

**Gifts = free items.** Alliance gift chests generated by spenders are a major non-spender source of sculptures, keys and VIP points [A06-0516]; their VIP items range from 10 to 1,000 points [A05-0004].

**Your side of the deal:** press help on other members' jobs every day (20 helps = 10 Daily Objective points) [A10-0006], and gather inside the territory.
why_md: New players often treat the alliance as a chat room. Mechanically it is a time saving on every timer that can be helped, a gathering bonus and a stream of free items. That is why every early guide says to join an active one first [A06-0516].

title: Days 15–21 goals: streaks, gems to VIP, the VIP Shop, one commander
body_md:
**Goals**
1. **Keep the VIP streak unbroken.** From streak day 9 it pays the maximum of 200 points a day [A05-0003].
2. **Put free gems into VIP points, not into finishing timers.** The majority advice is VIP 6 first (permanent second builder), then VIP 10; one source disagrees and says not to spend gems on VIP at all [A05-0008, A04-0009].
3. **Visit the VIP Shop every week** (Shop building, CH5, weekly restock). From VIP 2 it sells 100-AP items for 12,000 food (30 per restock); from VIP 3, 5-minute universal speedups for 7,000 food (50 per restock) [A04-0007]. These cost food, not gems.
4. **Pick one commander and finish him before starting others** [A06-0500]. Sun Tzu is the safest early choice because he needs no legendary (gold) sculptures [A06-0501]. Details: F2P guide (`d4-early-commanders`).
5. **Feed that commander from Daily Objectives**: the 100-point chest also holds 3 Epic Commander Sculptures and a Golden Key every day [A04-0001].
why_md: By now the daily routine exists; this stretch turns it into investment. VIP and one finished commander are where small daily inputs add up, while half-built commanders give little value [A06-0500].
uncertain_notes: Weekly sculpture income for a non-spender is unknown (L-A06-03), so we give no date for a finished commander.
low_spender_note: A Low spender reaches VIP 6 sooner, which frees the Builder Recruitment items; the commander advice does not change.

title: Concept for days 15–21: VIP
body_md:
**What VIP is.** An account level bought with VIP points. Each level has a threshold: VIP 1 needs 200 points, VIP 6 needs 11,500, VIP 10 needs 150,000 [A05-0001].

**Where points come from without paying:** the daily VIP chest streak (40 → 200 a day) [A05-0003]; gems at 1 gem = 1 point; the Alliance Shop; alliance gift chests; Mysterious Caves [A05-0004].

**What it gives that matters early.** VIP 6 makes the second builder permanent [A01-0006]. Each VIP level also has a free daily chest that grows with the level; from VIP 10 it holds one Legendary Commander Sculpture a day [A05-0006].

**How long it takes (derived, uncertain).** Assuming an unbroken streak and nothing else, the daily chest alone reaches VIP 6 around day 62; adding the 100 daily gems converted 1:1 brings it to around day 41 [A05-0007]. So for a pure non-spender, **VIP 6 lands after this guide's 30 days**: keep using Builder Recruitment items until then [A01-0006]. One-time gems (City Hall rewards, events, alliance-gift VIP items) bring the date forward [A05-0007].
why_md: VIP is the menu beginners most often misread: either as a pay-only feature or as something to ignore. It is a slow, permanent account upgrade that a non-spender also climbs, and its first big step (VIP 6) removes the second-builder chore [A01-0006].
uncertain_notes: A05-0007 is a derived estimate (low confidence) that assumes cumulative VIP thresholds (L-A05-01) and no other VIP sources. VIP point income from alliance gifts and caves is unmeasured (L-A05-03).
low_spender_note: Spenders also get VIP points from purchases; the official points-per-dollar table is not verified (L-A12-02).

title: Days 22–30 goals: the event calendar starts to matter
body_md:
**Goals**
1. **Open the in-game event calendar at every login.** Events don't follow a fixed schedule; the calendar shows upcoming events a few days ahead [A11-0512].
2. **Watch for More Than Gems.** Players report it about monthly, lasting 2 days, and only in kingdoms older than about 21 days [A11-0502]. It is the best window to spend gems, with an exception for players still below VIP 6 [A11-0502, A04-0009].
3. **Pioneer / Road to Revival (uncertain):** a single guide says it appears around day 20–23, and to buy the four gold keys first, then epic sculptures [A11-0510].
4. **Mightiest Governor (MGE):** take the individual milestone rewards; for a non-spender in a new kingdom the ranking is generally out of reach [A11-0500].
5. **Start a small hoard.** The majority advice is to save speedups, resource items and AP items for scored events and KvK instead of using them as they arrive [A11-0501]; Lohar's Trial is the event to save your first AP potions for [A11-0505]. The debate on speedups is in the F2P guide (`d41-speedups-spend-vs-hoard`).
why_md: Around the fourth week the kingdom's event cycle starts (More Than Gems needs a kingdom older than about 21 days [A11-0502]), and the value of what you saved begins to depend on timing. The calendar is the only reliable schedule [A11-0512].
uncertain_notes: A11-0510 (Pioneer timing and key advice) is a single low-confidence source. The More Than Gems cadence is a player-report working assumption (see A11-0502). The first day each event appears in a new kingdom is unmeasured (L-A11-01), and the current MGE format is a gap (L-A11-04).

title: Concept for days 22–30: events reward what you saved
body_md:
**One idea behind most events:** they pay for actions, at milestones or by score. Lohar's Trial pays for killing ordinary barbarians [A11-0505]; More Than Gems has daily milestones for gems spent [A11-0502]; MGE has individual milestone rewards [A11-0500].

**So timing changes value.** The same AP item or speedup is worth more when used inside the right event than on an ordinary day. That is the reason behind the hoarding rule [A11-0501] and the AP rule from days 4–7 [A09-0007].

**Calendar, not memory.** Event dates differ between kingdoms by age and Monument progress [A11-0512]. Don't rely on another kingdom's dates or on an old guide's day list.

**What comes after day 30.** The big cash-in of the hoard is Eve of the Crusade, the pre-KvK stage around day 85–95 [B01-0500, A09-0007]. See the F2P guide (`pk-eve-of-crusade`).
why_md: Beginners spend items as soon as they get them because the reward is immediate. Explaining that events multiply the value of the same item makes the hoarding advice understandable instead of arbitrary.

title: Open questions for the 30-day path (pending research)
body_md:
**Pending in-game measurement (T0) or research.** This guide avoids these numbers until they are measured:
- Which City Hall level a new player typically reaches on days 3, 7, 14, 21 and 30 (PROPOSED-CH-BY-KINGDOM-DAY).
- Minutes each daily task costs (L-A10-01).
- The current Daily Objectives task list after 1.1.09 (L-A10-02).
- Beginner protection and shield durations and prices (PROPOSED-SHIELDS).
- The day-by-day barbarian unlock schedule (L-A09-05) and the auto-peacekeeping unlock level (L-A09-04).
- The first day each event appears in a new kingdom (L-A11-01).
- Whether VIP thresholds are cumulative (L-A05-01), which changes the VIP date estimates.
why_md: A beginner cannot tell a measured number from a guess. Listing what is unknown keeps the guide honest and tells the research side what to measure first.
uncertain_notes: No cards: this block only lists gaps.
